title: Security gating and evidence traceability for Private deployments (SSO, RBAC, Audit, KMS/HSM)
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary: This ticket defines the product acceptance criteria, sign-off checklist, and evidence-traceability requirements for shipping the Private Deployment security surface: SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, role-based access controls (RBAC) for admin/operator roles, immutable audit logging and retention, and customer KMS/HSM integration and keys lifecycle. The goal is to produce a clear, testable gating flow for PM/Eng/Security/Legal sign-offs and to attach machine-readable evidence artifacts so sales/CS can satisfy enterprise auditors without ad-hoc engineering work.

Background and motivation: Enterprises evaluating Redwood Private consistently ask for (1) SSO + SCIM provisioning with enforced MFA and session controls; (2) fine-grained RBAC that isolates platform orchestration actions from runtime operations; (3) tamper-evident audit trails with retention controls; and (4) ability to integrate customer-managed keys (CMEK) backed by HSM for secrets at rest. Recent proposals from infra (ENG-3412) and runtime (ENG-3589) implemented the basic APIs, but PM needs to reconcile scope, acceptance criteria, and the final evidence artifacts required for sales/legal signoff.

Scope clarifications (in scope):
- SSO: Support SAML 2.0 (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows), OIDC optional, and SCIM v2 user/group provisioning with group-to-role mapping.
- RBAC: Role model with at least: Owner, OrgAdmin, PlatformOperator, DeploymentAdmin, ReadOnlyAuditor. Support role inheritance and explicit deny rules.
- Audit logs: Produce immutable logs with append-only storage, retention policy configurable per-customer, export to customer SIEM via syslog/JSON over TLS, and signed log digests for tamper detection.
- KMS/HSM: Support customer-provided KMS endpoints (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed keys for root encryption; rotation API and key-escrow controls for emergency access.

Out of scope: secrets scanning at rest for customer blobs, non-HSM vendor-specific features beyond standard KMS APIs, automated remediation workflows.

Primary success metrics:
- Security and Legal signoff obtained with a single evidence packet per customer onboarding 90% of the time.
- Audit-readiness: evidence artifact generation time < 2 hours for required items (logs, role mappings, KMS config).
- Integration test pass rate >= 95% across supported IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace) for SAML+SCIM flows.

Deliverables:
1) Product acceptance checklist and sign-off flow embedded in onboarding runbook.
2) Evidence generation tool (script + documented queries) that collects required artifacts into a time-stamped bundle.
3) UX/Console views for audit-log retention knobs and RBAC mapping.
4) PRD appendix with sample legal wording for customer contracts referencing CMEK/HSM controls.

Acceptance criteria: see field 'acceptance_criteria' below.

Risk and open questions:
- IdP variability: Some customers require non-standard SAML attributes (how to support without indefinite engineering scope?). Proposal: maintain a documented mapping guide and treat custom attribute adapters as paid Professional Services.
- Log immutability guarantees across on-prem storage: need to verify HSM-signed digests and retention on customer storage.
- Emergency key-escrow: legal constraints around forced-decryption requests need a playbook and POA definitions.

Stakeholders: PM (Aisha Patel), Security Eng (Lena Zhou), Infra Eng Lead (Marco Hernandez), Legal (Tom Rivers), Solutions Engineering (Priya Nair), Customer Success (Elliot Wu).
acceptance_criteria: SSO: Demonstrable SAML 2.0 SP support with test IdP profiles for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace (automated tests pass in CI).
SCIM: Automated provisioning of users and groups from IdP; group->role mapping applied within 5 seconds of provisioning event in test environment.
RBAC: Console shows role assignment UI; API validates deny overrides; test matrix validates that PlatformOperator cannot access DeploymentAdmin-only routes.
Audit logs: Logs are written to append-only store, accessible via console and exportable to SIEM; signed digest available for the retention window and verified by Security Eng.
KMS/HSM: Customer can register an external KMS endpoint and perform a key rotation without service downtime in staging (documented rollback steps).

Evidence bundle: The evidence generation tool produces a timestamped artifact containing (a) role mappings, (b) sample audit queries for a 24-hour window, (c) KMS config snapshot, (d) SAML metadata exchange logs — and a Security Eng confirms artifact validity.
Sign-offs: All stakeholding teams (PM, Security, Infra, Legal, Solutions Eng, Customer Success) explicitly sign the checklist and leave a timestamped comment in the ticket.
signoff_steps: PM validates acceptance criteria and confirms test matrix coverage.
Security Eng performs threat review and confirms tamper-evidence approach (signed digests) meets baseline.
Infra Eng validates production-grade KMS integration and key rotation playbook.
Legal reviews CMEK/HSM contract language and approves onboarding clause.
Solutions Eng conducts a dry-run onboarding with a sandbox customer and attaches the evidence bundle.
Customer Success approves the runbook / support matrix and confirms operational handoff.
Final: PM posts a consolidated sign-off comment and transitions ticket to 'Done'.
decisions: Adopt SAML 2.0 as the minimum viable SSO protocol; OIDC optional for future iteration.
Treat custom IdP attribute adapters as billable professional services rather than product scope.
Require signed log digests (HMAC or asymmetric signature) as the minimum tamper-evidence mechanism for Private deployments.
Expose KMS endpoints via a standard connector (AWS/GCP/Azure) and require customers to supply minimal service principal credentials for key usage; no customer key escrow by default.
notes: Conversations with Sales show customers frequently ask for a single PDF evidence packet during procurement — implement evidence bundle export in console.
Infra will add an API endpoint to return current role mappings and KMS config snapshot (ENG-3589).
Security prefers asymmetric signatures for digest signing; performance impact evaluated by ENG on 2026-02-11 and deemed acceptable for retention windows <= 2 years.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Marco H.: Spiked an HSM-signed digest prototype; included perf numbers in ENG-3589. Need to confirm storage adapters for on-prem customers.
2026-02-12 - Lena Z.: Security review pending for emergency key-escrow language. Recommend adding explicit POA requirement if we accept requests for customer key access.
2026-02-13 - Aisha P.: Updated acceptance criteria to require evidence bundle; moved ticket to 'Planned' pending Infra test runs.
